text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a development practice where team members integrate their code changes frequently, often several times a day. Instead of waiting until the end of a project, every change is automatically verified through a CI pipeline. This pipeline typically starts with an automated build, which compiles the code and ensures it can be packaged correctly. Following the build, a series of automated tests run, checking everything from basic functions to complex interactions. The main goal is catching issues early, before they grow into larger, more difficult problems. By providing immediate feedback, CI helps teams maintain a stable codebase, collaborate more smoothly, and deliver software with greater confidence.
